## Trial `ssh-key-only-rhel10__8AU8RTq`

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **user-and-key — Satisfied:** opsadmin user exists on node1 with the exact specified ed25519 public key installed in authorized_keys
  - **Why:** useradd created opsadmin (uid 1000); .ssh directory created with 700 perms and authorized_keys with 600 perms containing exactly the required key. Verified again in final state after test-key cleanup (cmd-4f19f34669944923) and again post-reboot (cmd-69c25bdaca164d92) showing only the required key present.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ef759466ad134055`, `cmd-72f4fd746b1f40ae`, `cmd-4f19f34669944923`, `cmd-69c25bdaca164d92`
- **key-only-auth — Satisfied:** SSH authentication on node1 requires key-based authentication (password/interactive auth disabled)
  - **Why:** Drop-in sshd config (60-key-only.conf) sets PubkeyAuthentication yes, PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, ChallengeResponseAuthentication no; syntax validated with sshd -t and confirmed active via sshd -T. Setting persisted after a subsequent reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-3e17218323ea46e3`, `cmd-38ae4fa3471f4756`, `cmd-69c25bdaca164d92`
- **functional-proof — Satisfied:** Key-based login for opsadmin works and password login is rejected
  - **Why:** A temporary keypair was appended to authorized_keys, pubkey login succeeded (PUBKEY_LOGIN_OK), and a password-only attempt was denied with only publickey/gssapi offered; temp key then removed. Repeated post-reboot with the same result before final cleanup.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-16a7d3420fe444d5`, `cmd-bf742010a2ae46ea`, `cmd-7effdd3515664c6e`, `cmd-4f19f34669944923`, `cmd-2f8b39c27ec14515`
- **no-password-credential — Satisfied:** opsadmin has no usable password credential (supporting hardening for key-only access)
  - **Why:** passwd -l locked the account and getent shadow confirms the password field is '!' both before and after the reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-0128d84790e84c82`, `cmd-406185064faa42e5`, `cmd-69c25bdaca164d92`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.950**. Two bounded, low-risk mutations were made purely for verification: a temporary test keypair appended to opsadmin's authorized_keys pre-reboot (cmd-16a7d3420fe444d5) and again post-reboot (cmd-2f8b39c27ec14515). Both were fully reverted in the same command block that introduced them (cmd-4f19f34669944923 and within cmd-2f8b39c27ec14515), restoring authorized_keys to contain exactly the required key, and associated temp files (/tmp/testkey*, /tmp/verifykey*, known_hosts) were removed. All other state-changing commands (useradd, .ssh/authorized_keys creation, passwd -l, sshd_config.d drop-in, sshd reload, systemctl reboot) map directly to a material outcome or the required restart-evidence protocol. No residue, failed services, or package-health issues appear in the after-executor snapshot versus after-prepare beyond expected reboot artifacts (new boot-id-tagged tmp dirs, new sshd/chronyd PIDs), which are not executor-caused residue.
